summary: Milestone 7 (Functional Paragraph Framework) end-to-end acceptance PASSED against the public URL (https://dev-converse.preview.emergentagent.com). Backend: 6/6 pytest passes in /app/backend/tests/test_milestone7_paragraph_function.py (264s wall time, 4 live SSE turns + 2 fast CRUD smokes). Frontend: 5/5 UI checks passed. Coverage: (a) STRONG paragraph — the effective 'When a friend likes your post...' paragraph produced theory.paragraph_function.applies=true with a populated .purpose ('Appears to introduce or illustrate a concept — the thinness of online closeness'), intervention.type='invite_only' (honored, not restructured), no rigid template phrasing, no content-coaching phrasing. (b) WEAK paragraph — the four-scattered-sentences draft ('Social media is bad. Also teens use it. Phones are expensive. Friendships matter.') was correctly diagnosed with pf.purpose='Unclear — sentences do not cohere around one job; no discernible function...' and pf.coherence='No controlling idea; sentences scatter across social media, phones, cost, and friendships.', with the invitation asking the student to name/decide what the paragraph is trying to do — no rigid template imposed, no content coaching. (c) M6/M7 coordination — the kitchen/cigarettes narrative paragraph yielded cp.primary='narrate' AND pf.applies=true with narrative-appropriate purpose ('Establish a charged moment of entry — or refusal to enter — into a space associated with someone who...'); NO persuasive-thesis push (no 'thesis statement', 'make a claim', 'state your argument', 'your argument'). (d) M5A regression — intervention.focus='writing' on every ordinary paragraph draft (4/4), intervention.writing_not_content_check populated in every case, no content-coaching red flags on any invitation. (e) M1-M6 regression: multi-turn writing->revise->answer preserves theory_history v1..v3 with prior versions intact (verified: theory_history[0].currently_relevant_domains == [], theory_history[1] == rel1, theory_history[2] == rel2); currently_relevant_domains stayed at 2 across all three turns ('Central Claim / Thesis', 'Paragraph Purpose'); intervention sequence was instruct_then_invite (turn 1: scattered draft) -> consolidate (turn 2: real revision producing a focused claim paragraph) -> invite_only (turn 3: student explains their move) — the intended Recognize->Name->Understand->Use->Reflect loop. All turns completed under 120s (no 502). No stage/grade/level language. (f) Frontend: with ?dev + cleared localStorage the workspace loads directly (writing-area visible, no Teacher Setup gate); submitting the strong paragraph via continue-button produced an ai-invitation within ~60s; open-dev-panel-button opens the Development Panel showing both the Communicative Purpose block (primary=persuade, secondary=[interpret, analyze], inferred_from populated, uncertainty populated) AND the new PARAGRAPH FUNCTION (M7) block with all five rows populated (purpose, contribution to whole, coherence, development='Illustration...', placement); new-test-session-button correctly resets the workspace to empty writing-area with no ai-invitation. Screenshot captured (/tmp/m7_devpanel.png) shows both blocks side by side in the panel.

action_items: None blocking. Milestone 7 acceptance holds end-to-end. All six M7 acceptance criteria verified: (a) paragraph_function.applies+purpose populated on both strong and weak paragraphs, (b) no rigid paragraph templates (PEE/PEEL/MEAL/RACE/topic-sentence+evidence+analysis/must-end-with-concluding-sentence all absent), (c) coherence and development read relative to purpose, (d) M5A focus='writing' + writing_not_content_check preserved, (e) M6 communicative_purpose.primary still populated (persuade / narrate / etc.), (f) frontend paragraph-function-block and communicative-purpose-block both render.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py — ParagraphFunction model (lines 134-143) and DevelopmentalTheory.paragraph_function field (line 150) are correctly wired with a default_factory that gives every new session an applies=False empty PF object. Verified via GET on a fresh session: pf.applies==False, pf.purpose='' as expected.

server.py — FUNCTIONAL PARAGRAPH FRAMEWORK block in SYSTEM_MESSAGE (lines 284-290) is crisp: (i) frames the paragraph as a FUNCTIONAL unit, not a template, (ii) enumerates the four M7 dimensions (PURPOSE relative to M6, FUNCTIONAL COHERENCE, DEVELOPMENT as resources not required components, RELATIONSHIP TO THE WHOLE), (iii) explicitly forbids obligatory topic-sentence->evidence->analysis->concluding-sentence, (iv) the applies-reliability fix (lines 289-290) works — even a strong paragraph gets applies=true with the function named. Verified live on 4 paragraph drafts: applies=true in 4/4 cases, purpose non-empty in 4/4.

server.py — _compact_theory (lines 384-398) correctly surfaces paragraph_function.model_dump() into the per-turn prompt, which is what lets multi-turn reasoning carry forward paragraph analysis. Verified in the multi-turn test: pf.purpose persisted meaningfully across writing->revise->answer.

server.py — theory output schema for paragraph_function (line 336) is well specified: it tells the LLM applies MUST be true only when a paragraph is under discussion, requires all five sub-fields when applies=true, and requires them empty otherwise. The LLM honored this on every observed turn.

M7/M6 coordination is empirically strong: on the narrative kitchen/cigarettes paragraph the engine set cp.primary='narrate' AND pf.purpose='Establish a charged moment of entry... into a space associated with someone who...' — the paragraph's purpose was read RELATIVE to the narrative communicative purpose, not forced into a persuasive frame. No 'thesis statement' or 'make a claim' phrasing leaked into the invitation.

The multi-turn intervention arc on the weak-paragraph -> revised-focused-paragraph -> student-answer path was exactly what the DEVELOPMENTAL INSTRUCTION LAYER prescribes: instruct_then_invite (introduce the concept of paragraph purpose) -> consolidate (name the developmental change after the real revision) -> invite_only (student has appropriated the concept). This is the Recognize -> Name -> Understand -> Use -> Reflect loop firing on paragraph-function work, not just thesis work. Nice validation that the layer generalizes.

frontend/DevelopmentPanel.jsx — paragraph-function-block (lines 201-228) correctly gates rendering on theory.paragraph_function?.applies. When applies=true the block renders all five fields with the same visual grammar as the Communicative Purpose block (purpose in amber, other fields in neutral). Verified in the browser: on the strong paragraph draft the block populates purpose/contribution/coherence/development/placement fully. The applies=false gating is also correct — no empty M7 block clutters the panel when there is no paragraph in focus (e.g., a thesis-only session).

rca of the issue: No functional defect observed. One noteworthy behavioral observation: the ?dev preset in App.js sets current_writing_task='Draft your essay.' (not 'Draft a paragraph.'), which the review request calls out. When I submitted a paragraph anyway (frontend test step), the engine correctly set paragraph_function.applies=true because it read the draft as a paragraph regardless of the task label — this is the intended M7 behavior (applies keyed off 'is a paragraph the unit in focus?' not off the task string). No action needed; the review request itself notes this and says 'for frontend just submit a single paragraph', which is exactly what I did. All acceptance criteria for M7 are met.
